The print is cut to the T-shirt's shape, so the shirt itself looks like the outfit being worn, with the sleeves as the outfit's sleeves. The outfit is printed across the whole front, over the shoulders and down both sleeves, showing a tweed jacket with chalk-dusted elbow patches. Front and back are both fully printed, the back showing how the same outfit looks from behind. The outfit's own cloth covers the whole shirt as one continuous print, so shoulders, sleeves and body are all in the outfit's colours. It is an ordinary T-shirt in shape, with a straight open hem and sleeves cut to match the outfit's sleeves. The printed top garment continues down the shirt to its straight hem, with at most a belt or sash at the waist. The outfit's collar meets the real collar band, its shoulders sit on the real shoulder seams and its sleeves fill the real sleeves, all in one piece of printed cloth. The uniform fills the whole straight-sided shirt shape edge to edge, the same width at chest, waist and hem. The shirt's sleeves are tailored to end at the elbow, exactly where the outfit's sleeves end. All textures, transparencies and sheens are printed patterns on solid cotton. The print is the garment itself, flat and unfolded over the shirt, in its own cloth and colours. It is a trompe-l'oeil T-shirt, a plain cotton shirt pretending to be the outfit. The tee is clearly a costume tee, not a plain shirt, it shows its pockets, flaps and trims, the headwear's emblem or crest worked into the chest and the outfit's badges, insignia and emblems, so anyone can tell at a glance what outfit it stands for. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed light tan skin tone.

The shirt's neckline is the outfit's collar opening, the shirt's sleeves carry the outfit's sleeves, and the shirt's hem is the outfit's lower edge, showing a silver robe with stars. The back of the shirt is printed just as completely, edge to edge, with the back of the same outfit, its back collar, shoulder blades and the backs of both sleeves. The outfit's fabric runs seamlessly over the shoulders and down the sleeves, every part of the shirt in the outfit's own colours and textures. It is an ordinary T-shirt in shape, with a straight open hem and sleeves cut to match the outfit's sleeves. Only the upper garment is printed, running all the way down to the shirt's straight hem. The outfit's collar meets the real collar band, its shoulders sit on the real shoulder seams and its sleeves fill the real sleeves, all in one piece of printed cloth. The outfit is stretched to the shirt's own straight-sided shape and fills it completely, so it suits any body size. A long-sleeved shirt is used so the outfit's long sleeves fit exactly, printed full length to the shirt's wrist hems. All textures, transparencies and sheens are printed patterns on solid cotton. Only the outfit's fabric, trims and fastenings are pictured, spread across the entire shirt as a continuous pattern. It also shows printed cuffs at the sleeve hems. The print wraps around the sides so the outfit seems to continue around the body. The tee is clearly a costume tee, not a plain shirt, it shows the collar, neckwear and fastenings of the outfit, the footwear's trim colours as stripes on the cuffs and hem and the held item or gear of the outfit, shown as a patch or large motif on the chest or a sleeve, so anyone can tell at a glance what outfit it stands for. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed light tan skin tone.

The outfit's front panels run straight down the shirt's front with its shoulders sitting on the shirt's shoulder seams, and its sleeves are printed along the shirt's sleeves to cuffs at the sleeve hems, showing a purple cassock with a cope and a pectoral cross. Turn the shirt around and the back carries the matching back of the outfit, printed edge to edge with nothing left plain. One continuous print of the outfit's cloth covers the shirt from collar band to hem and out to both sleeve hems. It is an ordinary T-shirt in shape, with a straight open hem and sleeves cut to match the outfit's sleeves. Only the upper garment is printed, running all the way down to the shirt's straight hem. The outfit's collar meets the real collar band, its shoulders sit on the real shoulder seams and its sleeves fill the real sleeves, all in one piece of printed cloth. The uniform fills the whole straight-sided shirt shape edge to edge, the same width at chest, waist and hem. A long-sleeved shirt is used so the outfit's long sleeves fit exactly, printed full length to the shirt's wrist hems. All textures, transparencies and sheens are printed patterns on solid cotton. Only the outfit's fabric, trims and fastenings are pictured, spread across the entire shirt as a continuous pattern. It also shows a printed collar around the real neckline. It is the kind of novelty tee that tricks the eye from across a room. To read as a costume rather than a plain top, it adds the belt, straps and buckles of the outfit, the outfit's badges, insignia and emblems and the held item or gear of the outfit, shown as a patch or large motif on the chest or a sleeve, bold and large enough to identify the outfit from across a room. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed light tan skin tone.
